articles: chicago newspapers to fight unions by engdahl in los angeles citizennational war against the newspaper printing trades by the national publishers association the anti labor organization of the nation s big daily newspapers is scheduled to break in chicago in 1915 that is the date of the expiration of the contract now held by the big chicago dailies with the typographical union which is to be made the chief object of attack it has been known for some time that the publishers were planning an anti labor crusade in an effort to establish the non union shop in the mechanical plants of the nation s daily press ever since the lockout in chicago in 1912 kept newspaperdom in a turmoil for almost a year there has been considerable speculation as to just when this campaign would be inaugurated it has now been learned from unquestionable sources that the long predicted open shop war against the newspaper trades which is now being planned and outlined will break less than two years hence moreover the newspaper kings expect to win they claim that it will be impossible for the organized workers to present a solid front in the struggle in support of this contention they point out how the typographical union declined to assist the other printing trades in the struggle last year they claim that labor will be divided that they will be aide to prevent the solidarity of the newspaper workers in 1915 as they have done in the past and that as a result victory will come easily in preparation for the pending struggle the chicago federation of labor will urge before the convention of the american federation of labor next month in seattle that every effort be made to wipe out all discord among the chicago newspaper workers growing out of last year s bitter dissension

better america federation s reactionary propagandaby paul scharrenberg secretary california state federation of labor miss hermine schwed field secretary of the national association for constitutional government is under the auspices of the better america federation addressing california women s clubs she is decidedly pro better america federation her latest effort is a widely published statement in which she warns the league of women voters against socialistic measures like the intiative and referendum it would be interesting to know the dictionary miss schwed uses or where she got the idea that the initiative and referendum are socialistic they are not so regarded in california here with a safe sane and conservative republican majority of 100 000 or more the initiative and referendum are considered sound republican doctrine the republican state convention of 1910 declared for direct legislation in the state and in the country and local governments through the initiative the referendum and the recall the democratic state convention of that year to make it unanimous declared for the initiative referendum and recall in state and local governments the republican governor elected that year in his inaugural address to the 1911 legislature recommended the initiative and referendum to preserve and perpetuate popular government that republican governor was later sent to the united states senate to carry republican california s conception of sound republican doctrine into national councils the republican legislature of 1911 in conformity with the declaration of the republican state platform and recommendation of the republican governor by a vote of 35 to 1 in the senate and 71 to 0 in the assembly proposed to the people of this republican state that they make the initiative and referendum part of their state constitution and the people did so by an overwhelming majority of 168 744 to 52 093 more than three to one miss schwed will scarcely hold that california was in 1911 three to one socialistic lost souls wandering in darkness however the lost souls wandering in political darkness out of which the better america federation was later formed don t like the initiative and referendum they have made frequent attempts to get the republican legislature of califonia to sanction changes in the state constitution that would render the initiative practically inoperative but the republican legislature refused to heed these constitution tinkers and refused to sanction changes in the constitution that would interfere with the practical and orderly process of the initiative failing in the legislature the constitution tinkers resorted to the initiative to limit the initiative in 1920 these opponents of the initiative invoked the initiative to submit an amendment to the constitution to the voters which had it been adopted would have seriously limited the use of the initiative and the voters of republican california cast 421 955 votes against such limitation although the anti initiative group carried on a costly campaign they succeeded in getting only 298 347 voters to back them up they were beaten by 123 598 majority surely miss schwed will scarcely claim there are 421 955 socialists in california or that california is socialistic by 123 598 majority constitution tinkers the constitution tinkers were not content with the drubbing they got in 1920 in 1922 they re opened their attack on the initiative and again by means of the initiative put an antiinitiative measure on the ballot again were they defeated by overwhelming majority they had succeeded in getting 298 347 votes against the intiative in 1920 they got only 258 009 against it in a falling off of 40 338 votes miss schwed will scarcely contend that out of more than a million california voters only 258 009 are opposed to socialistic policies in spite of the curious views of miss schwed in spite of the better america federation in spite of the constitution tinkers who have made repeated attacks upon the initiative and referendum provisions of our constitution california continues a safely republican state with a favorite son who makes the initiative and referendum one of the foundation planks of his platform well in the lead for the republican nomination for the presidency curiously enough miss schwed is advertised as field secretary of the national association for constitutional government her title is misleading it is difficult to reconcile it with her denunciation of provisions of our constitution as socialistic

by george r reilly commissioner reilly s column today is devoted to the answering of questions by readers on the series of articles he has written the fast several weeks about state government due to lack of space commissioner reilly will answer questions not included here direct to the individual by mail the concluding article appears next week editor q how much is the state tax on each gallon of motor fuel a three cents q how much of this goes to cities and counties a each city gets a half cent of every three cents collected as tax within its limits the same for each county q do all sellers of tangible personal property wholesalers manufacturers etc as well as retailers have to get a permit from the state board of equalization to do business a yes although sales tax is applicable only to retail sales exempting of course food and certain other commodities as prescribed by the act the permit costs $l oo q why is this permit necessary a principally so that the board may have accurate check on those required to pay sales tax to the state q ls it necessary to file a bond to insure sales tax payments a lt is the retailer can give his own security if he owns property or can post cash bond q ln what amount is bond required a ln twice the amount of the estimated sales tax due for the reporting period of payment q what records must be kept to comply with the sales tax law a records of all purchases and sales the retailer must have receipts of all purchases and complete records of all deductions for non taxable articles as well as a complete sales record q how long must these records be kept a until released by board authority q lf a retailer s permit is suspended is he out of business a he is and will be penalized if he continues q does the sales tax apply to my daily net or gross receipts a lt applies to gross receipts amounts of sales on exempt articles may be deducted before applying the 3 per cent sales tax but careful records of such exemptions must be kept q when are sales taxes payable to the state a the year is divided into quarters three month periods start ing january 1 hence the sales tax is due for the first quarter january february march on or before april 15 and the 15th of each month following the end of the other quarters failure to pay on time results in a penalty of 10 per cent of the amount due and interest charges of 4 per cent per month or fraction of a month failure to pay before another quarter is due may result in suspension or revocation of your permit then you re out of business q are any other arrangements made for sales tax payments a they can be paid weekly monthly or in the case of a temporary business when the business is closed q lf i post cash bond will i get it back when i go out of business a you will when sales tax due has been paid or deducted from the amount you have on deposit q what redress have i if your auditors check my records and disagree with me on the amount of tax paid a you may petition for a re assessment then if not satisfied you may ask for hearing before a referee representing the board he makes his recommendations to the board and if you re still not satisfied the board itself will give you a hearing q ls the board s decision final a yes but after paying the tax you may file a claim for refund and if it is disallowed by the state board of control you may sue in court for the refund q how does the board determine sales tax deficiencies a by careful audit of your books and records and by direct check on your business if the retailer has violated the law by not keeping proper records the board puts a direct check on his business for a given period and then arbitrarily levies taxes penalties and interest accordingly q suppose i disagree with this arbitrary assessment what can ido a here the burden of proof is on you and you must offer satisfactory records or evidence to prove error q has california a tax commission a ln theory no but the state board of equalization with its widespread tax administration serves in that capacity q who are the sales tax administrators in your district a burnett sheehan state building san francisco for san francisco and san mateo counties john j hayes 98 north first street san jose for santa clara santa cruz san benito monterey and san luis obispo counties q who is responsible for enforcing the alcoholic beverasre control act a officers of the alcoholic beverage control division of the state board of equalization and every peace officer of the state q does any of the beverage licensee fee money return to cities or counties a each city gets back half of the license fees collected therein each county gets back half the license fees collected in its unincorporated areas q what do they do with this money a for this answer i must refer you to your city council or county board of supervisors the understanding is at least part of this money be used by local authorities to help enforce the beverage control act the state force necessarily is limited because of the fact half of the license fees go back to the cities and counties and must look to local agencies for assistance q can a woman get a license to operate a liquor establishment a no new licenses for the sale of distilled spirits are being issued now because of the great number already in effect however sex is no deterrent if all other requirements are met under our existing laws q can a woman tend bar a only if she is a licensed operator or the wife of a licensed operator barmaids are taboo in california q can women employed as waitresses solicit drinks on a commission basis with the house a emphatically not these are what we call b girls and are not tolerated by the board over 21 but my wife isn t can buy her a drink in a liquor establishment a no and if you do you place yourself your wife and the licensed operator in line for criminal prosecution minors cannot be sold served or given alcoholic beverages in any licensed premises q can a minor work in a place where alcoholic beverages are served or sold a minors cannot work in on sale places where beverages are sold by the drink in any capacity having to do with such beverages the law says nothing about their employment in off sale places where alcoholic beverages are sold in the original package but not for consumption on the premises so it is presumed they may be employed therein q my husband is continually getting drunk on the money we need for living expenses what can i do to stop it a lf you find out where he buys his drinks you can forbid the licensed operator to sell to him the law says known drunkards cannot purchase alcoholic beverages if you fail to get cooperation write me at 200 state building san francisco giving the details your name and address and i ll see what i can do to help your confidence will be respectedq have cities or counties the right to adopt any ordinances pertaining to the use or sale of alcoholic beverages or the number or operation of places where they are sold a no the constitution vests sole authority concerning these things in the state q are slot machines or other gambling devices permitted in licensed premises a no gambling in any form is barred as is prostitution or any condition contrary to the public welfare and morals q lf i have a complaint against a licensed establishment to whom should i report it a telephone or write your nearest state board of equalization office or direct to san francisco headquarters 200 state building giving full particulars anonymous communications are not considered in good faith but every protection necessary will be given the names of those making such complaints if the situation is an emergency one call you local police q are men in uniform permitted to purchase drinks a yes however licensees are warned to give every cooperation to military and naval authorities and are specifically warned against buying or accepting government property in any form licensees are protecting themselves by this cooperation because the military can and does rule places of which they are suspicious out of bounds which prohibits any man in uniform from visiting them hence such places come under similar suspicion from the board and are liable to punitive action q do licensed alcoholic beverage establishments have to pay sales tax a yes the sales tax applies to them the same as to any other retailer q who are the chief liquor control officers in your district a don marshall 111 state building san francisco for san francisco and san mateo counties jerry o brien 98 no first street san jose for santa clara santa cruz san benito monterey and san luis obispo counties conclusion next week

asiatic exclusion leaguethe following is from the weekly news letter issued by the asiatic exclusion league those who favor importations of asiatic coolies in sufficient number to supply their own needs to be followed by as many more as may supply all other needs for cheap non assimilable labor will do well to give heed to the history of russia a nation that stands forth in the light of civilization convicted of being the great white criminal of the earth if the experience of a kindred people may ever light the footsteps of men then the experience of russia should be a warning to america to beware how it admits to its shores the evcr alien mongol the russian people were originally aryan they had the same origin as the people of germany and the low countries they were rather short of stature strongly limbed had high cheek bones broad high foreheads and up to the dawn of the thirteenth century were self governing and free but loosely connected as to communities not having evolved a national life capable of resisting a mongolian invasion under genghis kahn early in the thirteenth century this great mongolian conqueror with a force of 700 xh warriors swept russia nearly to the baltic destroyed free government and left a non assimilable host to amalgamate with the conquered people 1 here is a wonderful difference between assimilation and amalgamabou the jews whe ver they go assimilate readily with whatever civilization they encounter but amalgamate almost not at all the mongols on the contrary amalgamate readily where they go in considerable numbers acquire property and become fixed as they have done in many parts of the world and will do here in process of time but assimilate not at all they failed to assimilate in russia but amalgamated with hideous fecundity only mongolian men came and not their women and so they made themselves masters of the women of russia from this unholy and unfortunate alliance sprang the great mass of russian peasantry it is in the attempt to govern this amalgamated mass that russia has acquired the distinction of being the great white criminal of the civilized world the governing class is measurably if not entirely free from this contamination but it has been a superior race in charge of an inferior made inferior by amalgamation with a race alien in thought spirit antipodal in everything the result has been more unfortunate as it always is to the superior than to the inferior race the great hulking mass of stupid inert unimaginative peasantry is a bone of contention to be fought over by a divided aristocracy divided on an issue of human rights the mongrel mongolian looks on at the satanical carnival of assassination and repression with blinking unintelligent eyes caring little for consequences and enduring whatever befalls with a stoicism born of an oriental fatalism meanwhile the internecine conflict rages between those who have in their veins some survival of the free blood of their aryan progenitors and those who after 7 x years of dominance have come to believe in that mongolian absolutism that made genghis kahn the terror of europe and asia from pacific to baltic from arctic to india the fortunes of this war sway from extreme of hope to abandon of despair just now the reactionaries are in the ascendency and yet so permeated is the russian realm with the spirit of freedom that a douma selected by the reactionaries themselves has had to he purged by executions banishments and imprisonment without trial or semblance of trial the conflict is fratricidal and therefore waged with an intensity of bitterness otherwise unparalleled and although it is for and against the uplift of the great mongrel mass that mass lends little aid to its would be benefactors and only rages and ravages when it is hungry that is what amalgamation without assimilation means the mongol never assimilates but always amalgamates its product on this western coast would repeat what it has accomplished in interior russia the admixtures of blood would be essentially the same even though generations were required for its accomplishment whoever acts from impulses other than such as are afforded by present need will find the life line of the great white criminal nation terrifically illuminating no sooner are we supplied with everything the nature can demand than we sit down to contrive artificial appetites johnson

policy pursued in the construction of buildings president green said provides that the contract for the erection of government buildings shall be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder the too serious for triflinga situation far more serious than most people realize has been created by the present depression to trifle with the problem of unemployment or take advantage of the millions out of work for self enrichment at the present time is beginning to get more dangerous than it is to play with fire during the dry season while a restless wind is blowing it takes but a spark to start a devastating conflagration and many of the upheavals of history were started by a word or seemingly trivial incident when hungry people are roaming about in quest of work to get food and cannot find it they are not apt to be in any mood to be trifled with and given the ha ha by word or deed yet that is exactly what our politicians are doing these days when they make glowing promises before election that they have not the slightest intention of keeping in case they get in when men women and children are facing hunger and want although they are willing and able to work but unable to get employment while all about them they see the privileged few reveling in luxury and extravagance on wealth that they and their starving loved ones in many cases helped to create in the first place then such hard pressed people are liable to become desperate there are millions in the united states who find themselves in this woeful condition right now yet there are employers and people of great wealth whose greed for more is so abnormal that all they can see is that this condition of dire need is something they can take advantage of by reducing wages to increase their own profits if any considerable number of large employers were to join this wage cutting campaign our depression would be greatly deepened and prolonged and no one can fortell how serious a crisis might grow out of it gouging people may be a profitable business as long as those being gouged can be hoodwinked into standing for it but increasing the dose in the hardboiled manner that some of our profiteers want to do it these days is outright folly for people are rapidly developing an ugly mood and who would not be ugly when goaded by hunger while those who could relieve the situation just sit tight in order to increase their pound of flesh most of our politicians and a majority of our daily and weekly papers have been failing to give serious attention to the problem of unemployment or the other problems that confront the masses of our people who are hit the hardest by the present depression of course many of them have become so accustomed to giving the double cross to the rank and file of ordinary people that they imagine they can always get by with that kind of stuff this is exactly what those in control of every despotism that ever existed always thought up to the time when those in control were swept out of power and frequently they received pretty rough treatment while a change was being put into force and effect those who control political and industrial power in the united states today can ignore the needs of the growing army of unemployed and seek to capitalize on it by taking advantage of hunger to fatten their purses if they want to but the more of this that is done the nearer will they be bringing their own regime to the inevitable day of reckoning that no human tyrant can escape when conditions are ripe for his overthrow bunk and hypocrisy may have gotten by in the days of prosperity and plenty when everybody who wanted work could get some kind of a job but in the present day of widespread unemployment it will require some honest to goodness dealing and fair play to appease the growing discontent of the masses of the people if those in control today cannot develop a leadership that can and will take an intelligent lead in actually solving the problem of unemployment at the root then there must come a change for things cannot continue as they are without disaster on a national scale verily this is no time for trifling says the editor of the contra costa labor journal

woll says moderate wage increases and lower prices will prevent slumpwashington matthew woll of l vice president told a congressional committee that moderate wage increases coupled with price decreases are required to prevent economic recession and to restore the proper balance in price profit and wage relationships in testimony before the joint committee on the economic report mr woll said the american federation of labor is convinced that the feast and famine policy of american industry which in general has allowed prices and profits to climb to such unprecedented heights that consumer buying power is dangerously lagging will inevitably lead to economic recession unless corrective action is taken immediately we do not mean that in the case of each individual firm prices and profits are exorbitant while wages are depressed however when the actions of each segment of our economy are added up the aggregate figures have startling implications let me illustrate 1944 was the wartime highpoint in income payments to wage and salaried workers since that time wage rates have sharply risen but wage rates are illusory things because of downgrading shortened hours and shifts to lower wage industries average weekly earnings and total income payments in the form of wages and salaries dropped appreciably since that time average weekly earnings for factory workers were $47 50 in january 1946 the wartime peak after a severe drop from this level it was not until april of this year that average weekly earnings again reached this amount department of commerce figures indicate that income payments in the form of wages and salaries dropped from 116 0 billion dollars in 1944 to 105 2 billion dollars in 1946 a decline of 9 3 per cent but during this same period between 1944 and 1946 net income to proprietors jumped 25 3 per cent from 24 1 billion to 30 2 billion dollars interest and net rent jumped 22 6 per cent from 10 6 to 13 0 billion and net corporate profit jumped 21 2 per cent from 9 9 to 12 0 billion dollars these figures give some indication as to who was responsible for the increase in the consumers price index of 23 9 per cent between 1944 and may 1947 obviously we do not contend that business could operate without making a profit but we do contend that many segments of industry are following a price profit policy that is rapidly pricing their products out of the market and must inevitably lead to production cutbacks unemployment and eventual recession if business as a whole could realize such large profits in a year characterized by vexing reconversion problems and price controls during the better part of the year either profits must boom to unprecedented heights in 1947 with a consequent bust or a new lower price policy must be instituted with more reasonable profits but a continuing sjtrong stable mass market mr woll warned that food prices must come down if further pressure for wage increases is to be avoided pointing out that a wage earner spends ab ut a third of his income for food he said that additional food price increases will necessarily reduce demand for other goods this in turn will have serious implications for the maintenance of full production and employment

industrial news compiled l gt y the conciliation service during the past week the following adjustments of matters in controversy were reported building tradesman gary ind the department s representative who handled the case of the strike of building tradesmen at gary ind affecting 4000 men has wired that settlement has been made the plumbers inaugurated the strike after their demands for a wage increase had been refused and other building crafts struck in sympathy strike columbus ohio an interesting case is reported from columbus where a number of non union men refused to quit work on the neil house where they were engaged on a subcontract the conciliator representing the department wires as follows strike due to employment non union men on neil house settled in thirty minutes one hundred men struck four hundred preparing to quit department given full credit by both interests laborers boston and lowell mass the department s representative wires that the strike of laborers is about all that is left of the building trades dispute in boston and in new england the painters went back to work on may 27 having reached a decision to accept $l lo per hour until 1926 and arbitration thereafter the carpenters in the lowell district also returned to work on may 27 at the scale of $1 per hour until may 1 1926 when the rate will be increased to $l lo this strike was the first declared by this craft in twenty four years plumbers hazelton pa the strike of plumbers at hazelton pa which began may 1 has been settled these workers demanded an increase of lo i cents per hour and the master plumbers finally conceded the demand the new rate is $l l2 1 2 per hour other building trades have also signed for the coming year the strikes of carpenters and plumbers in the various cities of the middle anthracite district pending since may 1 have all been settled two commissioners of conciliation assisted in the settlements clothing workers goshen ind a strike of clothing workers at the plant of the cohen dress company of goshen ind has been settled according to a wire from the department s representative these workers demanded an increase of approximately 25 per cent which was refused the terms of settlement are not yet known longshoremen philadelphia pa the strike of 3000 longshoremen at philadelphia has been settled through an arrangement whereby the men return to work on the old basis with the promise that when the next agreement is made by the shipping board in other ports the same conditions will apply in philadelphia painters portland ore five hundred painters in portland struck for $9 per day and a five day week the strike becoming effective on may 15 a number of contractors have granted the wages demanded and the whole matter is in process of adjustment street car men akron ohio the street car situation in akron and vicinity has been cleared up the following lines were affected akron city lines canton city lines akron cleveland interurban and canton massillon interurban lines the demands were for a wage increase of 12j4 cents per hour and a readjustment of working conditions the persistent efforts of the department s conciliator to bring about an adjustment were rewarded with a satisfactory settlement working conditions were adjusted in conferences and the question of wages goes to arbitration about 750 men were directly involved children s garment industry new york the controversy affecting the children s garment industry of new york city and vicinity has been settled for the time being the contractors association had notified the manufacturers of children s clothing that a 10 per cent reduction in wages would become effective on may 11 when it was pointed out that the agreement under which the parties are operating does not expire until june 30 1925 the contractors association withdrew their demands they maintain however that in view of the dullness in this trade they are justified in old men for counsel a glimpse at our system of leaving the determination of fundamental laws to the wise men of the older generation editorial from the bulletin jan 27 the supreme court of the united states is composed of nine men whose average age is well over sixty years this court recently applied the terms of the sherman law to a labor union in the danbury hatters case although an act passed since the origin of this case specifically relieves unions of liability under that particular law the court has now put it beyond the power of any state to prohibit employers from exacting from men who work for them a pledge not to join labor unions or for that matter not to join churches or political parties or fraternal orders this decision wipes out an anti coercion act in kansas and probably similar laws in our own and other states the aggregate age of the supreme court is about 550 years when the court vas a child of 90 years and first went to school individualism untrammeled and unlimited was america s religion and rightly for the individual never had such an opportunity as was then presented to him on this continent the inclinations of a generation whether toward individualism or away from it usually fit the needs of that generation the court grew toward manhood and the dawn of its one hundred and eightieth spring found a downy fuzz upon its lip it was not meditating then on individualism or the law but walking rather on cool may evenings with dreamy eyed girls who are old now or dead these many years then the court said good by to these first loves and went to college where it frolicked and rollicked and as no doubt as gay as any college boy john d rockefeller sr was clerking in a grocery store not long before that time when the court left college being then toward the end of its third century it began to settle down and think seriously on the problems of life it married and had children and almost before it realized it had reached the end of its fourth century years flowed by the court grew gray haired lost the elasticity of its step and the elasticity of its thought grew less and less disposed toward the new theories that were making their way into the laws of the different states found it harder and harder to understand the tremendous changes that had come about the new inventions the rush of immigration the concentration of industry and wealth and fell back with an assured touch on the theories of life that were prevalent at the height of its manhood when its years were a scant four hundred there as something in the very atmosphere of the court s meeting place that seemed hostile to very new ideas this was natural it had been planned that way if the supreme court thus tended to fall behind the current thought of their fellow countrymen it was not from a lack in them of honesty or learning or reasoning power they are merely the exemplification of a constitutional system which leaves to old men the determination of legal principles which a generation of young men and men in the prime of life will have to live by the wonder is that these two labor decisions were not unanimous

$1 50 per yeargreen defends recovery act labor provisions must be strengthened to give toilers better protection of l chief tells senate committee real collective bargaining must be assured and code work week shortened to provide jobs for idle urges retention of service trades under nra jurisdictiona firm defense of the principles underlying the national industrial recovery act and the strong recommendation that it he strengthened and reenacted characterized the testimony given by william green president of the american federation of labor before the senate finance committee which was investigating the effects of nra codes although declaring that working men and women have not received as many benefits as they rightfully expected from the act and the codes established by its authority mr green insisted the thing to do was not to destroy the law and return to the jungle of unregulated industrial relations but rather to perfect it and make its basic principles valid in practice in addition to being commendable in theory he urged that additional legislation should strengthen the collective bargaining section of the act stressed the necessity of a work week shorter than the basic forty hours stipulated in most codes and emphatically opposed removing the so called service trades from nra jurisdiction importance of collective bargaining declaring that the national industrial recovery act is the first step in the establishment of real collective bargaining mr green said it had served a great purpose in this direction and must not be underestimated adding the nra has given millions of workers the legal right and the courage to organize for the first time in their lives it has made them feel free for the first time in their lives they will not see that right taken from them without a struggle on this most important phase of the new economic order instituted by the nra we need now to take the second step we need to strengthen and clarify the collective bargaining provisions of the act i have already urged that this can best be done by a federal statute as proposed by the wagner labor disputes bill a federal statute wi j extend the self organization and rrelective bargaining provisions of the recovery program to all employees collective bargaining must not be looked upon as an emergency measure only it must become a basic part of the changed economic order which is our ultimate aim shorter hours imperative stating that during the first stages of the nra the codes and the president s reemployment agreement had reduced the number of jobless from 14 000 000 to 11 000 000 mr green claimed this experience amply proved that the unemployed can be provided with jobs by reducing the hours of work that there are still many millions of unemployed is not proof against the soundness of the principle he said it is rather proof only that we have been too hesitant and timid to reduce the hours of work sufficiently to absorb a major portion of the unemployed hours of work have been fixed by most of the codes at forty per week that is too long a work week in view of the present technological and managerial development of industry protection for service trades mr green emphatically condemned the proposal made to the committee that the so called service trades should be dropped from the jurisdiction of the nra claiming that the trades employ between 2 000 000 and 3 000 000 men and women he charged that they are among the most exploited and poorly paid groups of workers in the entire country i say now he declared that labor will never willingly see them denied the protection given to all other workers and will oppose with all the force at its command any attempt to limit the nra in such a way that these millions of men and women will be without any regulation as to their wages hours and working conditions it is squarely up to the federal government to chart the course which is to be followed the formation of policy must be centralized under the national recovery administration it is not my province to discuss the legal basis for the protection of these workers it is my firm conviction however that some method can and must be found whereby they shall be covered by codes experiment must continue in concluding his argument in favor of legislation continuing the national recovery act mr green said no one would urge tearing down the foundations of a great bridge or dam on the theory that it should be destroyed because it was not yet a completed structure yet there are those who urge that a great social and economic experiment be scrapped because it has not reach completion in the short space of two years labor is not so impatient labor recognizes that social progress is a slow and unending task and that no worthwhile venture should be abandoned until there has been every opportunity for a thorough trial

the union manwho is he how can you recognize him what are his distinguishing traits guy e miller tells us he carries a paid up card as evidence of his membership in the union of his trade or industry that is a means of identification the fellow who never contributes anything to the cause of unionism yet insists that he is just as good a union man as those who do is a fraud a real union man attends the meetings of his organization whenever possible he knows that his union is a business institution to aid the worker in maintaining and improving conditions he docs not expect a business to run itself he gives his time his thought and his money to the cause the cause of unionism does not suffer reproach because of his conduct he studies the history of the labor movement in order that the present may avoid the mistakes of the past and also to be able to point out the contributions of the labor movement to the cause of human freedom he keeps up with the chief movements the trend of legislation and judicial decisions so that he may he able to intelligently aid whatever is helpful to labor s cause and oppose that which is injurious he exhausts peaceable methods of redressing grievances before advocating or resorting to a strike realizing that whatever contributes to the establishment of amicable relations between the employer and the employe promotes the well being of labor that an unnecessary strike whether lost or yon injures labor s cause when the strike is on he lends his fullest support to it he claims the enjoyment of his rights as a citizen but is wary of the emissaries of violence he places the facts before the people as a brief for the strikers cause outside the strike zone he is active in their behalf and pays his quota as an investment for improved conditions the union man is a thinking worker putting in practice the gospel of brotherhood exchange

allen of can t strike fame finally sent to private lifewashington the defeat of senator allen of kansas in the recent election is significant allen was appointed by the governor of kansas to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of senator curtis who was elected vicepresident allen when governor of kansas secured the passage of an anti strike law and inflamed the nation s non thinking element with his plea that the rights of the public are greater than the rights of individuals under this reasoning workers have no right if it interferes with popular inconvenience allen debated this question in new york city with the late samuel gompers allen s theory was upheld in the senate by sherman of illinois myers of oregon poindexter of washington and others long since forgotten allen is the last to join these ranks during his short stay in the senate he was considered spokesman for the administration and was a leader in the effort to secure senate approval of judge parker s nomination for supreme court justice his defeat was one of the election sensations he ran 25 000 behind george mcgill democrat while senator capper republican candidate for the full term was elected by more than 100 000 majority never in the history of kansas were organized workers so solidly lined up against a candidate wichita allen s home town which is republican rejected the man who would handcuff workers by more than 5 000 votes
